policies.name: goose
policies.summary: Use AI however you like with no disclosure needed, but review the code yourself before submitting.

policies.name: alacritty
policies.summary: No content from language models in code, docs, issues, pull requests or comments.

policies.name: Alamofire
policies.summary: Every PR states how much AI helped; PR descriptions must be human-written; AI translation is allowed.

policies.name: opencode
policies.summary: Long AI-generated PR descriptions and issues may be ignored; explain changes briefly in your own words.

policies.name: gumroad
policies.summary: Every PR ends with an AI disclosure naming the model and prompts; current frontier models are recommended.

policies.name: Mindustry
policies.summary: No AI-generated PRs or posted text; AI may review or translate, and AI-sourced findings must be marked.

policies.name: arrow
policies.summary: Linked guidance accepts AI PRs if you say what was generated and review it; disengaged PRs get closed.

policies.name: kafka
policies.summary: Add a Co-Authored-By or Generated-by commit trailer naming the AI tool; the human author stays responsible.

policies.name: pulsar
policies.summary: A human must review, submit and own AI-assisted changes; fully autonomous agent PRs are not acceptable.

policies.name: appwrite
policies.summary: AI does not lower the bar: you own the PR and review agent output against AGENTS.md.

policies.name: ruff
policies.summary: Follows Astral's policy: AI coding allowed, but comments and PR text are human-written; no autonomous agents.

policies.name: uv
policies.summary: Follows Astral's policy: AI coding allowed, but comments and PR text are human-written; no autonomous agents.

policies.name: Avalonia
policies.summary: AI-assisted PRs accepted when a human fully understands them; autonomous agents are not; keep descriptions short.

policies.name: bevy
policies.summary: Linked policy tolerates careful AI coding with disclosure; AI must not write docs, issues or PR prose.

policies.name: biome
policies.summary: Disclose any AI assistance and its extent; do not use AI to write PR descriptions or communication.

policies.name: ripgrep
policies.summary: AI coding is welcome, but comments and PR explanations must be human-written; autonomous agents are not allowed.

policies.name: caddy
policies.summary: AI-assisted code is fine, but every account must disclose LLM use; no automated interactions with people.

policies.name: clap
policies.summary: AI coding needs maintainer permission on the issue first and disclosure; comments must be human; no autonomous agents.

policies.name: ClickHouse
policies.summary: Embraces AI for development with optional disclosure; review generated code and own it like hand-written code.

policies.name: vinext
policies.summary: Built almost entirely by AI; contributors are encouraged to use AI, and every PR gets AI review.

policies.name: coolify
policies.summary: AI is allowed; mention any AI use in the PR and understand and verify every change.

policies.name: crewAI
policies.summary: AI-authored PRs and issues must carry the llm-generated label or may be closed without review.

policies.name: curl
policies.summary: AI-assisted code accepted at normal standards; reports from AI tools must say so and be verified first.

policies.name: sdk
policies.summary: Review all AI code, make sure it builds and passes tests, understand it, and verify AI-written text.

policies.name: deno
policies.summary: AI tools carry no penalty, but their use must be disclosed in the PR description.

policies.name: detekt
policies.summary: AI-assisted PRs are fine; work that looks entirely AI-generated with little human review is treated differently.

policies.name: directus
policies.summary: AI-assisted code allowed if fully understood; no autonomous agents; no wholly AI-written issues, PRs or comments.

policies.name: duckdb
policies.summary: AI coding is welcome, but comments and PR explanations must be human-written; autonomous agents are not allowed.

policies.name: pi
policies.summary: AI-written code is fine if you understand it; issues should be in your own voice or labelled.

policies.name: elasticsearch
policies.summary: Do not paste LLM output into PR descriptions or use LLM tools to talk with maintainers.

policies.name: elixir
policies.summary: Agents only for issues labelled Contributions Welcome or accepted features; disclose AI with an Assisted-by tag.

policies.name: otp
policies.summary: Issues must be created by humans; AI may help draft an issue you have reviewed yourself.

policies.name: eslint
policies.summary: AI-generated PRs must be disclosed and target accepted issues; maintainers expect human replies to feedback.

policies.name: expo
policies.summary: Name the AI tool in the PR, edit agent drafts yourself, and never let agents open PRs alone.

policies.name: flutter
policies.summary: Review and understand AI code, verify AI-written text, and never let AI replace human discussion.

policies.name: nao
policies.summary: AI-written code is fine if understood; state the model used and write the PR blurb yourself.

policies.name: llama.cpp
policies.summary: AI code allowed with disclosure and thorough manual review; AI must not write issues, PR text or replies.

policies.name: whisper.cpp
policies.summary: No mostly AI-generated PRs; AI may only assist human-written code, with disclosure; no AI-written posts.

policies.name: ghostty
policies.summary: All AI use must be disclosed and fully understood; AI-generated media is banned; slop authors get denounced.

policies.name: spec-kit
policies.summary: AI is encouraged, but disclose tool, model, settings and extent; agents label every commit and comment.

policies.name: gleam
policies.summary: Contributions from AI agents are not accepted; bug reports, PR descriptions and comments must be human-written.

policies.name: gitea
policies.summary: AI help is welcome with clear disclosure; review and test it, and don't rely on AI for replies.

policies.name: hugo
policies.summary: Disclose substantial AI use; AI contributions from non-maintainers must stay narrow, such as bug fixes.

policies.name: grafana
policies.summary: AI help is fine if you review, test and understand everything; keep pull requests focused and small.

policies.name: greptimedb
policies.summary: AI-assisted PRs need end-to-end understanding of the design, with uncertain AI-written parts flagged for reviewers.

policies.name: obscura
policies.summary: AI-assisted contributions are fine; low-quality or unreviewed agent output will be closed.

policies.name: terraform
policies.summary: Disclose the role AI played; PR descriptions must be human-crafted; no submissions from bot accounts.

policies.name: hono
policies.summary: AI may be used, but contributions that waste maintainer time can be closed and accounts blocked.

policies.name: immich
policies.summary: Do not open LLM-generated PRs or post LLM-written descriptions or comments; translation is acceptable.

policies.name: julia
policies.summary: Disclose substantive generative AI contributions with details, review every change, and open PRs yourself.

policies.name: starlette
policies.summary: You may use AI tools but stay responsible for every contribution; duplicate PRs lead to bans.

policies.name: uvicorn
policies.summary: You may use AI tools but stay responsible for every contribution; duplicate PRs lead to bans.

policies.name: kotlinx.coroutines
policies.summary: LLM output only for trivial, single-obvious-way changes; non-trivial code and discussion must not be LLM-authored.

policies.name: ktor
policies.summary: Any tool with human review; label substantial generated content; never use AI for comments or reviews.

policies.name: browser
policies.summary: AI-assisted or AI-driven PRs are welcome; summarize in your own words and discuss large changes first.

policies.name: llvm-project
policies.summary: Any tool with a human in the loop; label substantial AI content; no unapproved agents or good-first-issue fixes.

policies.name: localsend
policies.summary: AI-generated contributions are refused unless they are bug fixes, very small, or from proven experts.

policies.name: okhttp
policies.summary: No LLM-generated code, docs or communication; only disclosed translation and local autocomplete are allowed.

policies.name: retrofit
policies.summary: No LLM-generated code, docs or communication; only disclosed translation and local autocomplete are allowed.

policies.name: mastodon
policies.summary: Linked policy discourages AI; disclose significant use; no AI-written PR descriptions or comments; no autonomous agents.

policies.name: medusa
policies.summary: AI may help write code, but PR descriptions and replies to reviewers must be in your words.

policies.name: meilisearch
policies.summary: AI-generated content is not considered in external contributions, including code, tests, docs, PRs and issues.

policies.name: TypeScript
policies.summary: Fully agent-written patches are fine if understood and disclosed; bulk autonomous agent PRs are never accepted.

policies.name: mlx
policies.summary: AI-assisted coding is allowed; you stay accountable and must refine output to reflect your understanding.

policies.name: moby
policies.summary: Disclose tools and extent in the description, add a Created with note, and review AI content first.

policies.name: kimi-code
policies.summary: AI-assisted PRs meet the same standard as hand-written ones; understand and explain what you submit.

policies.name: n8n
policies.summary: AI-assisted work welcome if you understand every line; write descriptions yourself; disclosure encouraged, not required.

policies.name: nats-server
policies.summary: AI-assisted code accepted if understood and tested; communicate in your own words, not through an AI.

policies.name: nautilus_trader
policies.summary: AI help allowed with full human review; disclosure not required; no autonomous agent actions or AI co-authors.

policies.name: neovim
policies.summary: Review and refine AI output before requesting review; no one-shot AI PRs; cut verbose AI text.

policies.name: server
policies.summary: Disclose AI with Assisted-by trailers; descriptions and replies in your own words; no autonomous agents.

policies.name: node
policies.summary: AI allowed with disclosure and verification; no automated PRs, AI good-first-issue fixes or wholly AI-written messages.

policies.name: nuxt
policies.summary: AI welcome under two rules: write comments, issues and PR descriptions yourself, and understand what you submit.

policies.name: obs-studio
policies.summary: All code, descriptions, issues and comments must be human-written; assistive AI such as Copilot is heavily discouraged.

policies.name: ocaml
policies.summary: Write or personally review every part; disclose significant AI-generated code, descriptions or comments and the tool.

policies.name: openclaw
policies.summary: AI and vibe-coded PRs are first-class with no disclosure needed; show evidence and understand the code.

policies.name: openssl
policies.summary: Non-trivial AI portions need an Assisted-by trailer naming agent and model, plus a CLA with AI clauses.

policies.name: oxc
policies.summary: Disclose AI use and review and test everything; repeated low-quality AI PRs lead to bans.

policies.name: penpot
policies.summary: Responsible AI use is supported; AI-assisted content must be human-reviewed and verified before submission.

policies.name: pnpm
policies.summary: Agent-made PRs welcome if understood and tested; agent-written PRs, issues and comments need a disclosure footer.

policies.name: polars
policies.summary: No agent interaction; disclose all AI use; AI code only for accepted issues and never good first issues.

policies.name: postgrest
policies.summary: Adopts Gentoo's policy, which forbids contributing anything created with AI language tools.

policies.name: posthog
policies.summary: AI is fine if you understand and test the work; disclose agent involvement in the PR template.

policies.name: prettier
policies.summary: Submit only code you understand and have tested, follow the templates; low-quality AI content is closed.

policies.name: orm
policies.summary: No AI disclosure asked; results are verified, and an agent skill describes the contribution workflow.

policies.name: prometheus
policies.summary: AI bot PRs need a human owner or two maintainer approvals; every change gets two human reviewers.

policies.name: requests
policies.summary: LLM tools allowed if you own every line; no LLM co-author tags, unsupervised agents or LLM review comments.

policies.name: pydantic
policies.summary: AI use welcome if you fully understand the code; spammy or incoherent AI PRs may be closed.

policies.name: pytorch
policies.summary: AI-generated content in PRs, issues and comments must be labelled and explained; no fully autonomous agents.

policies.name: qdrant
policies.summary: Write the PR motivation yourself; disclose AI-made commits and the initial prompt; you own the result.

policies.name: quarkus
policies.summary: AI may assist if you understand and own the results; unsupervised bots and copied AI output are unacceptable.

policies.name: ray
policies.summary: Linked guidance requires PRs to state AI assistance and test results; agent-only PRs are not allowed.

policies.name: RxJava
policies.summary: Disclose any AI use in the PR, even for discussion only; you answer for whatever the LLM produced.

policies.name: rollup
policies.summary: AI-created PRs are fine, but maintainers may then edit them freely without prior discussion.

policies.name: llama_index
policies.summary: Highlight where AI wrote code and how you verified it; prefer AI for small, well-tested changes.

policies.name: cargo
policies.summary: Follows Rust's LLM policy: disclosed, pre-arranged LLM-created PRs only; no LLM-written comments, issues or descriptions.

policies.name: rust
policies.summary: LLM-created PRs need disclosure, a pre-agreed reviewer and non-critical scope; LLM-written comments and descriptions are banned.

policies.name: rustlings
policies.summary: LLM-generated code must be disclosed; using LLMs to write comments, issues or PR descriptions is banned.

policies.name: scala3
policies.summary: AI-assisted code accepted with full responsibility; all issues, PRs and discussions must be entirely human-written.

policies.name: serverpod
policies.summary: AI-assisted PRs are fine if you understand and validate them and answer reviewer questions personally.

policies.name: fd
policies.summary: Disclose AI use and extent; review generated code yourself; PR descriptions and comments must be human-written.

policies.name: spring-framework
policies.summary: AI agent contributions accepted with careful human review; accounts run by autonomous bots are banned.

policies.name: sqlalchemy
policies.summary: Using AI for help is fine, but don't post AI-generated text, even lightly edited; use your own words.

policies.name: sqlfluff
policies.summary: AI-assisted PRs welcome at the same bar; disclose material AI use and what you validated manually.

policies.name: starship
policies.summary: Every AI-assisted PR must disclose it; no substantial AI on good first issues; no autonomous agents.

policies.name: storybook
policies.summary: AI as a personal assistant is welcome; a real person opens each PR and discloses the tool.

policies.name: streamlit
policies.summary: Responsible AI use is welcome with full author ownership; outside pull requests are currently paused.

policies.name: ai
policies.summary: AI may generate code you understand, test and verify; mass low-quality AI PRs are treated as spam.

policies.name: query
policies.summary: AI may generate code you fully understand; comments, issues and PR descriptions must be in your voice.

policies.name: router
policies.summary: AI drafts are fine if reviewed and owned; agents are told to disclose authorship; no mass PRs.

policies.name: tauri
policies.summary: Review and test all LLM output before submitting; do not use AI to answer review comments.

policies.name: rich
policies.summary: AI-generated PRs accepted if labelled with the agent and linked to a maintainer-approved solution.

policies.name: textual
policies.summary: AI-generated PRs accepted if labelled with the agent and linked to a maintainer-approved solution.

policies.name: timescaledb
policies.summary: AI coding assistants are welcome; AI code meets the same standards and low-quality AI PRs are closed.

policies.name: vite
policies.summary: AI welcome under two rules: write comments, issues and PR descriptions yourself, and understand what you submit.

policies.name: vitess
policies.summary: AI-written code is fine if it reflects real work and understanding; AI-driven issue sniping is discouraged.

policies.name: vitest
policies.summary: AI may generate code you fully understand; comments, issues and PR descriptions must be in your voice.

policies.name: wagtail
policies.summary: Purely AI-generated work is unwelcome; disclose AI use and write the PR description yourself.

policies.name: warp
policies.summary: Any coding agent may implement contributions, with free cloud agents offered; talk to maintainers as a human.

policies.name: zed
policies.summary: LLM coding welcome with a human who understands it; no autonomous agents; don't let LLMs write your messages.
